review.tagline: NumPy-style array framework for machine learning on Apple silicon
review.summary: MLX is an array framework from Apple machine learning research with Python, C++, C and Swift APIs. It builds lazy, dynamic computation graphs, offers composable transforms for autodiff and vectorization, and includes PyTorch-like mlx.nn and mlx.optimizers packages. Arrays live in unified memory, so CPU and GPU ops share data without copies. Linux CUDA and CPU-only packages exist.
review.audience: ML researchers and engineers training or running models on Macs
strengths: Python API follows NumPy; mlx.nn and mlx.optimizers follow PyTorch
Unified memory: CPU and GPU ops share arrays without transfers
Composable transforms for autodiff, vectorization and graph optimization
Python, C++, C and Swift APIs; installs via pip on macOS and Linux
weaknesses: Designed for Apple silicon; Linux CUDA and CPU backends are add-on installs
Example models live in a separate mlx-examples repo
Supported devices are only CPU and GPU per the README
Model zoo and ecosystem size compared to PyTorch not stated in README
needs: Models: LLaMA, Stable Diffusion, Whisper, LoRA fine-tuning
